data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"On clear, calm nights, urban thermal mass dominates the UHI: daytime heat stored in masonry and asphalt is released as sensible heat after sunset, and the cross-city gap scales with built density and impervious surface fraction.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If rural thermal mass (e.g., bare rock or dry soil) is comparable to urban thermal mass, the storage-release advantage vanishes.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If anthropogenic heat release or cloud cover dominates the nocturnal energy balance, thermal-mass storage is not the primary mechanism.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If advection or wind speed is high, stored heat is dispersed before it can sustain a localized UHI.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"High heat-capacity materials absorb solar radiation during the day and convectively transfer stored sensible heat to the air at night, slowing the urban cooling rate relative to the countryside; cities with greater thermal mass and impervious area exhibit a larger nocturnal temperature gap.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
